raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I have been farming this same land in Quzhou my whole life. My mother farmed it before me. Everyone here grows wheat in winter and corn in summer — that is what this land is for, what the seasons allow, what the markets buy. I do not know other crops. I would not risk my family's income on something new.

For wheat, I will go to the village supply station and buy the seed they recommend — they have always given us a good variety, something like Ji Mai or Zheng Mai. I do not save my own wheat seed anymore because the bought seed performs better; my neighbor told me this and she is right.

For corn, I always buy hybrid seed from the market in town. Everyone uses Zheng Dan 958 or something like it. It yields well.

For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer before planting and then add urea when the plants need it — at jointing for wheat, at tasseling for corn. I use a generous amount. When I was younger and used less, the yield suffered. I would rather use a bit more than lose the harvest.

Wheat needs water three times: after sowing, at jointing, and before heading. If summer is dry I will irrigate the corn once or twice. We pump from the groundwater well.

I spray for aphids and powdery mildew on wheat. The shop in town tells me what to buy.

I use a rotary tiller before planting wheat. For corn, I plant directly into the wheat stubble with a seeder — fewer steps, less work, and the soil holds moisture better.

My land is about 10 mu total. I split it evenly.
